evidence.text: The inspected entry calls 北 a *huiyi* graph resembling two people back-to-back and the original graph for 背 (“back/turn against”). It reports Shang oracle use borrowed for the north direction, citing inscriptions 合集8783 and 合集32030. The author says frequent use for north led to the later addition of 肉 in 背, leaving 北 chiefly for north. Printed page number 726 is visible in the scan; the entry is on PDF page 739. The cited inscription contexts were not independently checked here.
evidence.title: 字源

evidence.source: Zhengzhou University Center for Chinese Character Civilization, Chen Anqi
evidence.text: The study describes the form from Shang inscriptions through the Shuowen seal form as two people back-to-back, with changes in stroke execution. It proposes an original word meaning “turn against/violate,” while acknowledging no secure excavated example has been identified; two proposed Zhouyi examples remain uncertain. This is an interpretation of the graphic conception and later written evidence, not a demonstrated earliest spoken sense.
evidence.title: “北”字职用演变研究（一）

evidence.source: Zhengzhou University Center for Chinese Character Civilization, Chen Anqi
evidence.text: The author reports 北 used from the Shang period as a loan graph for the direction “north,” its continuing principal function. The study distinguishes this from proposed extensions of an inferred “turn against” word. Thus the graphic history, a proposed original word sense, and the attested use of the graph for north are separate claims.
evidence.title: “北”字职用演变研究（三）

evidence.source: Zhengzhou University Center for Chinese Character Civilization, Chen Anqi
evidence.text: The study reports 北 used for “back” in Qin–Han manuscripts while the graph 背, formed with 肉 as semantic element and 北 as phonetic, emerged around the Qin–Han transition. An early Western Han Zhangjiashan manuscript still uses 北 more often for “back”; by Eastern Han evidence 背 is the usual graph. This describes writing practices, not the origin date of the spoken word.
evidence.title: “北”字职用演变研究（一）

evidence.source: Zhengzhou University Center for Chinese Character Civilization, Chen Anqi
evidence.text: The author proposes paths from “turn against” to bodily back and back side, and further to concealment, betrayal, abandonment, military defeat/flight, and defeated troops. The article provides Qin–Han manuscript examples for bodily back and back side and discusses other excavated or transmitted examples. Some steps rely on transmitted-text spellings or proposed semantic links; this evidence does not establish a complete chronology of spoken senses.
evidence.title: “北”字职用演变研究（一）
